chapter: Touring, band and money in the 1950s-60s
title: Clubs played in New Orleans in the 1950s
summary: He names the Showboat on Bourbon Street, Pete's Paradise and Club Tijuana, and says he never played Robin Hood.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What are some of the clubs you played at in New Orleans?
I played at the show bar on Bourbon Street. I called her two sisters. How about back in the 50s?
In the 50s. When you were recording the check right now. Dewdrop. Yeah, Dewdrop.

There was a club on the corner of Drys and… Flosses? No. They tore it down. Pete's Paradise. In fact, I named the place. It's Pete's? Pete's Paradise. And, um, Club Tijuana. Club Tijuana. No, I never played at Robin Hood. You never played at Robin Hood? No. That was before my time. That was way before my time. I played at Fosters.
